prerequisites: Having completed and passed 'Thermal Engineering' and 'Fluid Mechanics' courses from the second year
Knowledge of Thermal Engineering and Fluid Mechanics

learning_outcomes.text: Students must have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the cutting edge of their field of study.

Students must know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students must be able to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students must be able to transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Students must have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Ability to work, lead and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels and fluid systems.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Laboratory practice: Study of a steam power plant
Laboratory practice: Gas mixtures without reaction. Psychrometric diagram
Laboratory practice: Study of a cooling tower
Laboratory practice: Study of heat exchangers: tube-in-tube, plate, and shell and tube
Modeling of thermal systems with PC

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Theoretical exam)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (Directed work on thermal modeling)
Laboratory/field practices/use of ICT tools (Completion of laboratory practices)

assessment_rules: The global grade consists of 70% from a content exam (including exercises and questions) and 30% from continuous assessment activities. Both the exam and the continuous assessment blocks must be passed separately to contribute to the final grade. A minimum score of 5 points (50%) is required to pass the content exam. Continuous assessment activities must also be passed during the academic period; however, the specific weights for the individual continuous assessment components are not unambiguously stated or may vary.
